citation: Wu et al. Adaptation in protein fitness landscapes is facilitated by indirect paths. eLife. doi:10.7554/eLife.16965
question: How does high-order epistasis affect accessible adaptive paths?
main_result: Reciprocal sign epistasis blocks many direct paths while indirect paths can bypass traps.
limitations: Retrospective landscape study; not a low-budget adaptive controller.
relation_to_our_claim: Defines the oracle and motivates diversity/local-search comparisons.

citation: Romero et al. Navigating the protein fitness landscape with Gaussian processes. PNAS. doi:10.1073/pnas.1215251110
question: Can uncertainty-aware surrogate models guide efficient protein search?
method: Gaussian processes with Bayesian decision-theory design algorithms
experimental_budget: Small iterative experimental designs; budget differs by experiment
main_result: GP uncertainty supported informative and optimization-focused experimental search.
limitations: Different protein representation and no same-surrogate adaptive-policy-switch ablation.
relation_to_our_claim: Establishes uncertainty-aware sequential protein design as prior art.

citation: Wu et al. Machine learning-assisted directed protein evolution with combinatorial libraries. PNAS. doi:10.1073/pnas.1901979116
question: Can MLDE outperform conventional directed-evolution search?
system_or_dataset: GB1 retrospective landscape plus enzyme wet-lab campaign
method: Panel of supervised models trained on assayed combinatorial variants
experimental_budget: GB1 simulations and plate-sized wet-lab designs; not the proposed 96-assay four-round protocol
acquisition_strategy: Top predicted variants after model training
main_result: ML-guided combinatorial screening found higher-fitness variants than comparator DE approaches.
limitations: Does not isolate dynamic strategy allocation from surrogate/model choice.
relation_to_our_claim: Strong direct prior art against any claim that ML guidance on GB1 is new.

citation: Biswas et al. Low-N protein engineering with data-efficient deep learning. Nature Methods. doi:10.1038/s41592-021-01100-y
question: Can useful fitness models be learned from very few assays?
method: Pretrained sequence representation plus low-N supervised learning
primary_metric: Activity and diversity of nominated variants
main_result: Low-N models screened large in-silico spaces and nominated diverse active variants.
limitations: Not GB1; not a controlled adaptive acquisition-switching study.
relation_to_our_claim: Supports the small-data premise but not the agentic contribution.

citation: Wittmann et al. Informed training set design enables efficient ML-assisted directed protein evolution. Cell Systems. doi:10.1016/j.cels.2021.07.008
question: How do training-set design and encoding affect MLDE on epistatic landscapes?
system_or_dataset: GB1 and other public combinatorial landscapes
method: MLDE and focused-training MLDE with zero-shot prescreening
experimental_budget: Includes 24 or 48 training variants within total burdens near 80 and larger
acquisition_strategy: Predicted-mean exploitation after fixed training-set design
main_result: Training-set design and hole avoidance dominated many model/encoding effects and improved low-burden outcomes.
limitations: Uses privileged zero-shot predictors in some conditions and does not test evidence-driven switching among primitives.
relation_to_our_claim: Critical confound warning: controller comparisons must share initialization and candidate information.

citation: Yang et al. Active learning-assisted directed evolution. Nature Communications. doi:10.1038/s41467-025-55987-8
question: Can iterative batch Bayesian optimization improve epistatic protein engineering?
system_or_dataset: Wet-lab ParPgb plus GB1 and TrpB simulations
method: Iterative retraining with greedy UCB or Thompson-sampling acquisition
experimental_budget: GB1: 96 initial plus four rounds of 96; wet lab used larger batches than OmniEvo
acquisition_strategy: One acquisition function is selected for a campaign; surrogate is updated each round
adaptive_or_fixed: Sequential but acquisition policy is fixed per evaluated condition
primary_metric: Normalized terminal maximum fitness; wet-lab yield/selectivity
main_result: ALDE outperformed average DE/random in simulations and improved a wet-lab catalyst over multiple rounds.
limitations: Substantially larger budget; compares fixed acquisition functions rather than a matched controller that reallocates slots among multiple primitives after critic feedback.
relation_to_our_claim: Highest novelty-overlap risk; forces OmniEvo claim to focus on same-surrogate dynamic allocation under 96 total assays.

citation: Rapp et al. Self-driving laboratories to autonomously navigate the protein fitness landscape. Nature Chemical Engineering. doi:10.1038/s44286-023-00002-4
question: Can a closed-loop autonomous laboratory engineer proteins?
system_or_dataset: Glycoside hydrolase thermostability and P450 surrogate validation
method: SAMPLE robotic design-build-test-learn platform with multi-output GP
experimental_budget: Less than 2 percent of its defined landscape; not the 96-assay GB1 protocol
acquisition_strategy: Bayesian optimization balancing exploration and exploitation
main_result: Four autonomous agents found thermostable enzymes in closed-loop wet-lab campaigns.
limitations: Different protein/library/budget; no adaptive-versus-fixed same-surrogate allocation ablation.
relation_to_our_claim: Autonomous protein engineering is established prior art; Omnigent orchestration alone is not novel.

citation: Singh et al. A generalized platform for AI-powered autonomous enzyme engineering. Nature Communications. doi:10.1038/s41467-025-61209-y
question: Can a general biofoundry run autonomous multi-round enzyme engineering?
method: Protein language model initial design; low-N supervised iteration; automated biofoundry; LLM component
experimental_budget: Four rounds and fewer than 500 variants per enzyme
main_result: Reported large activity improvements over four automated rounds.
limitations: Different biological systems and much larger budget; allocation-policy contribution is not isolated.
relation_to_our_claim: Shows agent/automation claims must be narrowed to the controlled policy-value experiment.

citation: Xu et al. ProteinMCP: An agentic AI framework for autonomous protein engineering. Protein Science. doi:10.1002/pro.70547
question: Can an LLM orchestrate heterogeneous computational protein-design tools?
system_or_dataset: Fitness modeling binder design and nanobody workflows
experimental_budget: Workflow-dependent; not a fixed assay-budget landscape benchmark
primary_metric: Workflow completion time and case-study outputs
main_result: Demonstrated end-to-end computational protein workflows and tool orchestration.
limitations: Primarily computational design; does not test dynamic assay allocation on hidden GB1 against matched fixed policies.
relation_to_our_claim: Direct prior art for agentic protein-engineering orchestration; avoid first-agent claims.

citation: Prasanna et al. Coevolution-informed Bayesian optimization for sample-efficient protein design. bioRxiv. doi:10.64898/2026.08.06.743295
question: Can a coevolution-informed representation improve low-budget Bayesian optimization?
method: DCA-informed latent landscape plus Bayesian optimization
experimental_budget: Reported virtual optimum within 40 evaluations on avGFP
acquisition_strategy: Fixed BO on a specialized representation
main_result: Reported strong sample efficiency from representation-induced smoothing.
limitations: Preprint; different landscape and representation; improvement may come from features rather than controller adaptation.
relation_to_our_claim: Reinforces the requirement to hold the surrogate and representation fixed in the primary contrast.
